message_1_subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call: SLO targets & GPU sizing
message_1_body:
Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the Dedicated capacity validation for Finlytics: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Primary workload: streaming chat assistant + batch reranking for nightly index refreshes.
- Targets: 95th pctl latency for streaming responses <= 150ms for short-turn exchanges (<=128 tokens); tail latency (99th) requirement around 400-500ms.
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency of ~20 concurrent active streams, peaks up to 60 during sudden spikes.
- Throughput: batch reranking jobs require ~300 qps equivalent during nightly windows; token throughput not sustained at peak daytime.
- Model family: preference for an open Llama-style 7B variant in fp16/4-bit quantized profiles; willing to evaluate one larger (13B) for quality/latency tradeoffs.

Asks we agreed to validate on Dedicated capacity:
1) Baseline latency & p95/p99 with 7B quantized model on two GPU types (A10G-equivalent and H100-equivalent) using your typical prompt distribution (I took the SLO matrix you shared and attached it).
2) Reserved throughput sizing to keep p95 <=150ms at 20 concurrent streams and headroom for 60 concurrent spikes.
3) Streaming behavior - ensure chunked tokens emitted at <=50ms intervals for perceived responsiveness.
4) Cost/throughput delta between GPU choices and recommended autoscale headroom.

Next steps (owners & timing):
- Finlytics: send representative prompt set + 2 sample transcripts and confirm quantization constraints (Priya) - due EOD Mon 11/24.
- Redwood (Aditya/Rafael): run benchmark matrix across A10G/H100-equivalent setups and return a short summary + recommended reserved sizing - deliver by Wed 11/25.
- Schedule a 30-min sync to review results and decision criteria Thurs 11/26.

Attaching: finlytics-slo-matrix.xlsx (your matrix), gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf (Redwood standard comparison).

If I've missed anything, flag it - otherwise we'll proceed to run the benchmarks once we have the prompt set.

Thanks,

message_2_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call: SLO targets & GPU sizing
message_2_body:
Thanks Marissa - appreciate the clear recap. A couple clarifications and the prompt set are attached.

Clarifications:
- The 150ms p95 target is specifically for the interactive streaming path where users type and expect near-real-time replies. For batch reranking, p95 can be relaxed to ~800ms as long as throughput is met during the nightly window.
- For streaming we care about perceived responsiveness: initial token latency (time to first token) should be <=75ms and then steady chunk emission every ~40-60ms.
- Concurrency note: 20 typical concurrent active users, but spikes to 60 occur for product marketing events; we'd rather provision reserved capacity to handle 30 steady and rely on burst for 60 if costs are prohibitive.

Attached: finlytics-prompt-set-v3.json (representative prompts), sample-transcripts.txt

If you can run the A10G vs H100 comparison with our prompt set (quantized 4-bit where possible) that'd be ideal. Also flag any model memory constraints for 13B if you test that too.

Thanks - Alex

message_3_body:
Looping in Rafael to own the benchmark runs. Quick notes before we start: 

- We'll run the following matrix: 7B-quantized on A10G-equivalent (cost-optimized) and H100-equivalent (latency-optimized); optional 13B-quantized on H100-equivalent if memory allows. Each run will simulate:
  * 20 steady concurrent streaming sessions (your steady-state)
  * load-tests for 30 and 60 concurrent sessions to observe p95/p99 and degradation behavior
  * batch rerank job simulation at target qps for nightly window (300 qps equivalent).
- Reserved sizing: we'll propose a conservative reserved pool to meet p95 <=150ms at 30 concurrent, and show what headroom is needed to sustain 60 with autoscale.
- Streaming metrics: time-to-first-token, inter-chunk latency distribution (median/95/99), p95/p99 request latency, and GPU utilization / memory footprints.

Deliverable: a 1-page summary + CSV of raw metrics and the recommended Dedicated configuration (GPU type, number of instances, target reserved throughput) by Wed 11/25 EOD. Rafael - can you confirm run start time?

message_4_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call: SLO targets & GPU sizing
message_4_body:
Alex - quick status update: we kicked off the benchmark runs this morning at 07:30 PT. Preliminary observations from the 7B quantized runs: 

- A10G-equivalent (cost tier): p95 for streaming at 20 concurrent = ~110-140ms depending on prompt length; time-to-first-token ~65-80ms. At 30 concurrent the p95 drifts to ~170-200ms on some prompt shapes. At 60 concurrent, p95 exceeds 400ms and GPU utilization is saturated.
- H100-equivalent (performance tier): p95 for streaming at 20 concurrent = ~75-90ms; time-to-first-token ~40-55ms. At 60 concurrent p95 remains under ~220-260ms with higher cost.
- 13B-quantized on H100: memory allows run in 4-bit for shorter context lengths; p95 at 20 concurrent ~120-160ms - good quality but higher cost and lower concurrency headroom.

Recommendation (initial): reserve a Dedicated pool sized for H100-equivalent capacity to comfortably meet the 150ms p95 target at 30 concurrent (this gives headroom for spikes to ~60 when combined with autoscale). If budget constraints require A10G, reserve sizing should target 30 concurrent but expect p95 tradeoffs during peaks and consider a fallback model variant for degraded latency.

I'll prepare the one-page summary and attach raw CSVs in the next update. Can we still meet Thu 11/26 10:00 PT for the results review?

--
Rafael Mendes
Performance Engineering - Redwood Inference
